types.necessity: L1.identity requires that a change to a trade does not make it a different trade; a value invariant across every report of the same trade is required to express that persistence, which is exactly the identity mutation role.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's trade number is never reassigned to a different trade; if a trade number were reused for a different trade this role would misidentify reports, which should trigger review.
types.review_trigger: the same trade_number value appears to identify two trades the business considers different

types.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires a trade to belong to the account it was placed under, and requires that a later change does not move a trade that was already placed; a value naming that account, set once and never replaced by a later report, is required to express that. L1.identity supplies the account's own persistent number as the value this reference carries. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome's 'leaves the ownership as first recorded' is the clause that, alongside L1.attribution-at-placement, makes this value's role frozen_from_first_encounter rather than mutable.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade's account assignment is settled at the trade's first-encountered report and never legitimately contradicted by a later report of the same trade.
types.review_trigger: a later report of a known trade names an account different from the one recorded at first encounter

types.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires the trade's placement to be the moment stated by the earliest report of it the brokerage holds, in that report's own recorded time -- across every anchored source of held reports, not only raw.trade_cdc; for a historical-load trade that is its earliest raw.trade_history row. L1.attribution-at-placement requires that a later change does not move a trade that was already placed; since this moment is what selects the account statement the trade references, it must be set once and never replaced, or a later report could shift which statement is selected and move the trade's ownership.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the earliest report of a trade the brokerage holds, across both anchored sources, states its own time, and that time is treated as the placement moment even when it is not the trade's true first lifecycle event (the first-seen-late case L1.placement-moment names).
types.review_trigger: a trade's first-encountered report, across both anchored sources, carries no determinable event time

types.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership to reference the account as it stood at placement, not merely which account; L1.as-of defines that answer as the account's statement whose effective_from is the latest at or before the queried moment; a dedicated value carrying that specific effective_from is required to complete the (account_number, effective_from) reference that identifies the exact account statement. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome states directly that a later report of the same trade 'leaves the ownership as first recorded'; on this entity (incremental_by_identity, not versioned), that reference is fixed once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report, which is exactly the frozen_from_first_encounter role -- not per_statement, which describes a value's own kept-history nature on a versioned entity, a role that belongs to the account entity this value is drawn from, not to how it behaves once pinned here.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.account entity carries a statement of this trade's owning account whose effective_from is at or before placed_at.
types.review_trigger: no logical.account statement of the trade's owning account has an effective_from at or before placed_at

types.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires that, through the account, the trade also belongs to the customer as that customer stood at the same moment; a dedicated value naming that customer is required to express that half of the clause. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome states directly that a later report of the same trade 'leaves the ownership as first recorded'; on this entity (incremental_by_identity, not versioned), that customer reference is fixed once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report, which is exactly the frozen_from_first_encounter role -- not per_statement, which describes the value's own kept-history nature on the account entity it is drawn from, not how it behaves once pinned here.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the account statement this trade's ownership pins has a resolvable owning customer.
types.review_trigger: the account statement this trade's ownership pins has no resolvable owning customer

types.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership reference to name the customer as they stood at placement, not merely which customer (already named by owning_customer_number) -- 'and through it the customer, as they stood at the moment the trade was placed'; L1.as-of defines that answer as the customer's statement whose effective_from is the latest at or before the queried moment; L1.placement-moment fixes that moment to placed_at. A dedicated value carrying that specific effective_from is required to complete the (customer_number, effective_from) reference that identifies the exact customer statement, fixed once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report -- frozen_from_first_encounter, not per_statement, which describes the value's own kept-history nature on the customer entity it is drawn from, not how it behaves once pinned here.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.customer entity carries a statement of this trade's owning customer whose effective_from is at or before placed_at.
types.review_trigger: no logical.customer statement of the trade's owning customer has an effective_from at or before placed_at

types.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires a trade whose first-encountered report is not its true earliest lifecycle report to be marked first seen late, so the ownership placement fixes can be reviewed; a dedicated value carrying that marking is required to express it. L1.attribution-at-placement's 'do not move a trade that was already placed' requires this marking, once made at first encounter, never to be reconsidered by a later report -- frozen_from_first_encounter, not mutable.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the anchored trade_code_meanings.status_order and report_order let this job determine, at first encounter, whether the trade's lifecycle appears to have started before that report.
types.review_trigger: a trade's first-encountered report, across both anchored sources, carries a status outside {PNDG, SBMT, CMPT, CNCL}, or the business states a trade legitimately first reported at SBMT (for example, a market order whose life does not begin at PNDG)

types.necessity: L1.placement-moment (amended) distinguishes a market order's first lifecycle event (SBMT) from a limit order's (PNDG); a dedicated value carrying which of the anchored trade_type_codes a trade is is required to determine that event, so the L3 audit can recompute first_seen_late without re-reading the raw feed for the type. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome enumerates exactly the outcome facts a later report changes (status, executed price, fees, commission, tax, quantity) and states that a later report leaves the ownership as first recorded; order type is in neither set, so nothing a later report does moves it -- frozen_from_first_encounter, not mutable, on the strength of that enumeration rather than of L1.attribution-at-placement, which is about the ownership reference, not this value.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while trade_code_meanings.trade_type_codes exhaustively enumerates the order types (TLB, TLS, TMB, TMS) and a trade's order type is fixed at first encounter and never changed by a later report.
types.review_trigger: a trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report carries a t_tt_id value outside {TLB, TLS, TMB, TMS}, or a later report of a known trade_number names a different order type than the one recorded at first encounter

types.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names status as one of the outcome facts that changes as a trade moves through its life (pending, submitted, completed, cancelled); a dedicated value is indispensable to express that fact, replaced by a later report rather than kept beside it.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's own status coding names the trade's current lifecycle stage on every report.
types.review_trigger: a trade report carries no determinable status value

types.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names executed price as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from any bid or requested price.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single executed-price value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.
types.review_trigger: a trade report carries more than one executed-price value, or the value recorded does not represent an executed price

types.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names fees as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from commission and tax.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single fees value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.
types.review_trigger: a trade report carries more than one fees value

types.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names commission as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from fees and tax.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single commission value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.
types.review_trigger: a trade report carries more than one commission value

types.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names tax as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from fees and commission.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single tax value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.
types.review_trigger: a trade report carries more than one tax value

types.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names quantity as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single quantity value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.
types.review_trigger: a trade report carries no determinable quantity value

entities.grain: one row per trade, identified by trade_number, updated in place by later reports that change its outcome facts and never change the frozen placement-moment ownership reference
entities.necessity: L1.identity requires a trade to be the same persistent identified thing across every report of it, not a new trade each time. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires that a later report of the same trade update its outcome (status, executed price, fees, commission, tax, quantity) in place. L1.attribution-at-placement requires that a trade's ownership, once established at placement, is never moved by a later change to the account or customer, and that nothing the trade created is moved either. Together these entail exactly one row per identified trade, updated in place by later reports, holding a portion frozen at first encounter beside a portion that mutates -- the incremental_by_identity history kind, not versioned (which would keep every report as a separate dated statement) and not append_by_identity (which would treat every report as a new, unrelated event).
entities.parallel_assumption: Credible while every raw.trade_cdc row, and every raw.trade_history row, for the same t_id/th_t_id is understood to be a later report about that same trade rather than a distinct trade reusing the number.
entities.review_trigger: a later raw.trade_cdc or raw.trade_history row for a known trade_number is found to describe what the business considers a different trade
entities.note: This entity's frozen portion carries the full reference L1.attribution-at-placement describes: which account (owning_account_number), which of that account's dated statements (owning_account_effective_from, as of placed_at), and through that statement, which customer (owning_customer_number) -- see sg.placement-moment. It also carries first_seen_late, marking a trade whose first-encountered report is not its true earliest lifecycle report, per L1.placement-moment and the anchored trade_code_meanings.status_order and report_order. L1.hole.owner-change-reversions-account is carried because, if its resolution means an owner-side change also re-versions the account, the specific account statement placed_at pins for a given trade could shift.

attributes.name: trade_number
attributes.necessity: L1.identity requires a value that identifies which trade a report is about and stays the same across every later report of that trade; this attribute carries the identity type for exactly that purpose.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's trade number is stable and unique per trade.
attributes.review_trigger: two reports with different trade_number values are claimed to be about the same trade, or vice versa

attributes.name: owning_account_number
attributes.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires a trade to belong to the account it was placed under and forbids a later change from moving it; this attribute names that account, set once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report. raw.trade_history carries no account field (th_t_id, th_dts, th_st_id, batch_date only), so regardless of which anchored source supplies placed_at, this attribute is still, and only, sourced from the trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report's t_ca_id.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the account a trade is placed under is settled at the trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report; whether a later report could legitimately correct it is not addressed by the clause and is not assumed here. A trade any of whose placement-fixing facts -- placement, owning account, or order type -- would come from a held report is held under L1.hole.held-first-report-placement until answered: the earliest report of the source that supplies that fact is held, whatever another source's earliest report says. Until answered, such a trade is unclaimed by this attribute -- it is held and reported by inv.unknown_codes_held (together with inv.trade_held_first_report_unclaimed), not given an owning_account_number value, and no logical.trade row.
attributes.review_trigger: a later report of a known trade_number names an account different from the one recorded at first encounter, or a persisted trade carries this attribute null, which inv.trade_ownership_pin_present names as a violation

attributes.name: placed_at
attributes.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires placement to be the moment stated by the earliest report of the trade the brokerage holds, in that report's own time; this attribute carries that moment, set once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report. The earliest held report may be a raw.trade_cdc row or, for a historical-load trade with anchored raw.trade_history rows, one of those instead; the two handoffs feeding this attribute together cover both anchored sources.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the trade's first-encountered report, across both anchored sources (raw.trade_cdc and raw.trade_history), states its own event time. A trade any of whose placement-fixing facts -- placement, owning account, or order type -- would come from a held report is held under L1.hole.held-first-report-placement until answered: the earliest report of the source that supplies that fact is held, whatever another source's earliest report says. Until answered, such a trade is unclaimed by this attribute -- it is held and reported by inv.unknown_codes_held (together with inv.trade_held_first_report_unclaimed), not given a placed_at value, and no logical.trade row.
attributes.review_trigger: a trade's first-encountered report, across both anchored sources, has no determinable event time

attributes.name: owning_account_effective_from
attributes.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the account to be referenced as it stood at placement, not merely named; together with owning_account_number, this attribute completes the (account_number, effective_from) pair that identifies the specific account statement in effect at placed_at, per L1.as-of's 'latest statement that took effect at or before' the queried moment.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.account entity carries a statement of this trade's owning account with an effective_from at or before placed_at; not yet resolvable where the correct statement is one of ownership-history's own deferred CDC-sourced account statements.
attributes.review_trigger: no logical.account statement of the owning account has an effective_from at or before placed_at, or more than one candidate ties for latest, or a persisted trade carries this attribute null, which inv.trade_ownership_pin_present names as a violation

attributes.name: owning_customer_number
attributes.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires that, through the account, the trade also belongs to the customer as that customer stood at the same moment; this attribute carries that customer directly from the same account statement owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from already pin, so it can never name a customer inconsistent with that statement.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the account statement pinned by owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from has a resolvable owning_customer_number.
attributes.review_trigger: the account statement this trade's ownership pins has no resolvable owning_customer_number, or a persisted trade carries this attribute null, which inv.trade_ownership_pin_present names as a violation

attributes.name: owning_customer_effective_from
attributes.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership to reference the customer as they stood at placement, not merely which customer -- 'and through it the customer, as they stood at the moment the trade was placed'; together with owning_customer_number, this attribute completes the (customer_number, effective_from) pair that identifies the specific customer statement in effect at placed_at, per L1.as-of's 'latest statement that took effect at or before' the queried moment, and L1.placement-moment's fixing of that moment.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.customer entity carries a statement of the customer named by owning_customer_number with an effective_from at or before placed_at; not yet resolvable where the correct statement is one of ownership-history's own deferred CDC-sourced customer statements.
attributes.review_trigger: no logical.customer statement of owning_customer_number has an effective_from at or before placed_at, or more than one candidate ties for latest, or a persisted trade carries this attribute null, which inv.trade_ownership_pin_present names as a violation

attributes.name: first_seen_late

derivation.rule: null when the trade is held for review, not decided either way: its first-encountered report's order_type (t_tt_id) is outside the anchored four codes (TLB, TLS, TMB, TMS), its first-encountered report's status (th_st_id or t_st_id) is outside the anchored four codes (PNDG, SBMT, CMPT, CNCL) -- either held under L1.unknown-codes, reported by inv.unknown_codes_held -- or it is a market order (TMB, TMS) whose first-encountered report is PNDG, held under L1.hole.market-order-seen-pending and reported by inv.trade_market_order_seen_pending_held. Otherwise: true when the trade's first-encountered report -- across both anchored sources, per trade_code_meanings.report_order (the earliest raw.trade_history row if any exist for the trade, otherwise the raw.trade_cdc row with the smallest (batch_date, cdc_dsn) for that t_id) -- carries a status later, in trade_code_meanings.status_order (PNDG, SBMT, CMPT, with the terminal CNCL treated as later than any of them), than the order's first lifecycle event; false when it carries exactly that event. The order's first lifecycle event is read from order_type (this entity's own attribute, handed off from the trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report's t_tt_id): PNDG, status_order's first entry, for a limit order (TLB, TLS); SBMT for a market order (TMB, TMS), per L1.placement-moment's amended sentence that an order sent straight to market has no pending stage. Not received from any source; computed once, at first encounter, by comparing that report's own status against the order type's first lifecycle event where the trade is not held, and left null where it is.

attributes.necessity: L1.placement-moment (amended) requires a trade whose first-encountered report is later than its true first lifecycle event to be marked first seen late, so the ownership placement fixes can be reviewed, and states directly that an order sent straight to market has no pending stage and is not first seen late when its earliest report is submitted -- fixing a market order's first lifecycle event at SBMT. trade_code_meanings.status_order's first entry, PNDG, fixes a limit order's first lifecycle event; trade_code_meanings.trade_type_codes supplies only which codes exist and which are market or limit (TLB, TLS limit; TMB, TMS market), not either meaning. A first-encountered report whose status is later than that first lifecycle event is exactly such a trade (SBMT or later for a limit order never seen pending; CMPT or CNCL for either order type never seen at its own first stage). Two cases this clause does not decide are held rather than defaulted: L1.unknown-codes forbids interpreting a first-encountered report whose status or order type falls outside the anchored vocabularies, so first_seen_late is null for it (inv.unknown_codes_held reports the record); and L1.hole.market-order-seen-pending leaves undecided whether a market order first reported PNDG is a late first encounter, a mis-typed order, or a record error, so first_seen_late is null for it too (inv.trade_market_order_seen_pending_held reports the record). L1.attribution-at-placement requires this marking, once made (true, false, or held), to be fixed at first encounter and not reconsidered by a later report.
attributes.note: null means the trade is held for review, under L1.hole.market-order-seen-pending (a market order first reported PNDG) or under L1.unknown-codes (an unanchored order type or status on the first-encountered report); it is not a value first_seen_late asserts, only the absence of one pending review.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while every trade's lifecycle begins at its order type's first lifecycle event -- PNDG for a limit order, per status_order's first entry, SBMT for a market order sent straight to market, per L1.placement-moment's amended sentence -- and while trade_code_meanings.status_order, terminal_status_codes, and trade_type_codes exhaustively enumerate a trade's lifecycle statuses (PNDG, SBMT, CMPT, CNCL) and order types (TLB, TLS, TMB, TMS) with every trade report carrying one of each, except that a first-encountered report may carry a status or order type outside those vocabularies, in which case L1.unknown-codes holds the record for review (inv.unknown_codes_held) and this attribute is null rather than true or false; and while report_order correctly identifies the first-encountered report across both anchored sources (the earliest raw.trade_history row when any exist for the trade, otherwise raw.trade_cdc's (batch_date, cdc_dsn) ordering). raw.trade_history's anchored identifiers (th_t_id, th_dts, th_st_id) permit two of a trade's rows to share a th_dts with different th_st_id, which would make the earliest row's status -- and so first_seen_late -- ambiguous; this derivation assumes that does not happen. A market order first reported PNDG is likewise held, under L1.hole.market-order-seen-pending (inv.trade_market_order_seen_pending_held), rather than resolved by this derivation.
attributes.review_trigger: first_seen_late is found non-null for a trade held on its first-encountered report's status or order type (per inv.unknown_codes_held) or as a market order seen pending (per inv.trade_market_order_seen_pending_held), or null for a trade held on neither -- an unknown code on a later report does not hold the first-encountered report and does not make first_seen_late null

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.necessity: L1.placement-moment (amended) requires knowing whether a trade is a market or limit order to determine its first lifecycle event -- SBMT for a market order sent straight to market, PNDG for a limit order -- which first_seen_late's derivation needs; this attribute carries that order type directly from the trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report's t_tt_id, so the derivation, and an L3 audit recomputing it, need not re-read the raw feed for the type.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_tt_id on a trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report is the order's own type and trade_code_meanings.trade_type_codes exhaustively enumerates it (TLB, TLS, TMB, TMS). A trade any of whose placement-fixing facts -- placement, owning account, or order type -- would come from a held report is held under L1.hole.held-first-report-placement until answered: the earliest report of the source that supplies that fact is held, whatever another source's earliest report says. Until answered, such a trade is unclaimed by this attribute -- it is held and reported by inv.unknown_codes_held (together with inv.trade_held_first_report_unclaimed), not given an order_type value, and no logical.trade row.
attributes.review_trigger: a trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report carries a t_tt_id value outside {TLB, TLS, TMB, TMS}, or a later report of a known trade_number names a different order type than the one recorded at first encounter

attributes.name: status
attributes.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its status, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries status directly and is replaced by each later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while every trade report carries a determinable lifecycle status (pending, submitted, completed, or cancelled).
attributes.review_trigger: a trade report carries no determinable status

attributes.name: executed_price
attributes.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its executed price, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries executed price directly and is replaced by each later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own executed-price fact once the trade has executed; a report of a trade that has not yet executed may carry no executed price yet, which the clause does not forbid.
attributes.review_trigger: a trade report whose status the business considers executed or completed carries no executed price

attributes.name: fees
attributes.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its fees, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries fees directly and is replaced by each later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own fees fact once determinable; a report of a trade not yet executed may carry no fees value yet, which the clause does not forbid.
attributes.review_trigger: a trade report whose status the business considers executed or completed carries no fees value

attributes.name: commission
attributes.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its commission, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries commission directly and is replaced by each later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own commission fact once determinable; a report of a trade not yet executed may carry no commission value yet, which the clause does not forbid.
attributes.review_trigger: a trade report whose status the business considers executed or completed carries no commission value

attributes.name: tax
attributes.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its tax, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries tax directly and is replaced by each later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own tax fact once determinable; a report of a trade not yet executed may carry no tax value yet, which the clause does not forbid.
attributes.review_trigger: a trade report whose status the business considers executed or completed carries no tax value

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its quantity, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries quantity directly and is replaced by each later report.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while every trade report carries a determinable quantity, from the moment it is placed onward.
attributes.review_trigger: a trade report carries no determinable quantity

handoffs.necessity: L1.identity requires the trade's own number as its identity; raw.trade_cdc carries t_id as the brokerage's trade number on every row reporting that trade, including its first-encountered row and every later report.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_id values in this file are the brokerage's real trade numbers and not reused for different trades. A raw.trade_cdc row carrying any unknown code -- cdc_flag, t_st_id, or t_tt_id -- is held as a whole under L1.unknown-codes and supplies no fact to any handoff, not only this one; a trade whose every received report is held is not yet known to this job (inv.every_received_trade_persisted does not claim it). The hold is reported by inv.unknown_codes_held, not this handoff.
handoffs.review_trigger: a t_id value in this file is found reassigned to a different trade

handoffs.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's own account be named and fixed at first encounter; raw.trade_cdc's t_ca_id is the brokerage's own recorded account number on the trade's first-encountered report, and this handoff takes that value only, never a later report's t_ca_id, per the clause's 'do not move a trade that was already placed.' raw.trade_history carries no account field, so this remains the only handoff for owning_account_number even for a historical-load trade whose placed_at is instead pinned from a raw.trade_history row.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_ca_id on a trade's first-encountered report names the account the trade was placed under. A raw.trade_cdc row carrying any unknown code -- cdc_flag, t_st_id, or t_tt_id -- is held as a whole under L1.unknown-codes and supplies no fact to any handoff, not only this one; a held row keeps its place in the order of reports and can still be this trade's first-encountered report, holding the trade under L1.hole.held-first-report-placement without any of its content being read for this handoff's purposes, and a trade whose every received report is held is not yet known to this job. A trade any of whose placement-fixing facts -- placement, owning account, or order type -- would come from a held report is held under L1.hole.held-first-report-placement until answered: the earliest raw.trade_cdc report is held, whatever another source's earliest report says. Until answered, this handoff supplies no owning_account_number value for such a trade, which is held and reported by inv.unknown_codes_held instead, together with inv.trade_held_first_report_unclaimed.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_ca_id is found to record something other than the trade's owning account, or to change across reports of the same trade

handoffs.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires placement to be the moment stated by the earliest report of the trade the brokerage holds, in that report's own time. raw.trade_cdc's t_dts is that report's own recorded time; for a trade whose only held reports are Trade change records (every incrementally loaded trade, and any historical-load trade with no anchored TradeHistory rows), t_dts on the first-encountered such row is the earliest report the brokerage holds. For a historical-load trade with anchored raw.trade_history rows, the earliest held report is one of those instead (see the sibling handoff from raw.trade_history.th_dts), so this handoff and that one together, both under selector first_encounter_only, supply placed_at across the two anchored report sources; this handoff never takes a later report's t_dts.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_dts on a trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report is the report's own stated time of that event, not a receipt or batch-load time, and while, for a historical-load trade, any earlier-held raw.trade_history rows are correctly preferred by the sibling handoff instead. A raw.trade_cdc row carrying any unknown code -- cdc_flag, t_st_id, or t_tt_id -- is held as a whole under L1.unknown-codes and supplies no fact to any handoff, not only this one; a held row keeps its place in the order of reports and can still be this trade's first-encountered report, holding the trade under L1.hole.held-first-report-placement without any of its content being read for this handoff's purposes. A trade any of whose placement-fixing facts -- placement, owning account, or order type -- would come from a held report is held under L1.hole.held-first-report-placement until answered: the earliest report of the source that supplies that fact is held, whatever another source's earliest report says. Until answered, this handoff supplies no placed_at value for such a trade, which is held and reported by inv.unknown_codes_held instead, together with inv.trade_held_first_report_unclaimed. A trade whose every received report is held is not yet known to this job.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_dts is found to record something other than the report's own event time, or a historical-load trade's raw.trade_cdc row is used for placed_at despite anchored raw.trade_history rows existing for that trade with an earlier th_dts

handoffs.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires placement to be the moment stated by the earliest report of the trade the brokerage holds, in that report's own time. For a historical-load trade, the brokerage's held reports include its raw.trade_history rows (per-status reports, one per lifecycle stage) as well as its raw.trade_cdc snapshot row; the anchored trade_code_meanings.report_order states that such a trade's earliest held report is its earliest raw.trade_history row, not the snapshot. th_dts is that row's own recorded time, and this handoff takes it only from the trade's first-encountered raw.trade_history row (the one with the smallest th_dts), never a later one, and only when such rows exist for the trade.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while th_dts on a trade's first raw.trade_history row is that report's own stated time of that lifecycle event, and while every historical-load trade's per-status reports the brokerage holds are exactly its anchored raw.trade_history rows (none held but unanchored). raw.trade_history's own anchored identifiers are (th_t_id, th_dts, th_st_id), not (th_t_id, th_dts) alone, so the anchors permit two rows of the same trade to share a th_dts with different th_st_id; this handoff assumes that does not happen among a trade's rows, since two rows tied for smallest th_dts would make which one is 'the earliest' -- and hence first_seen_late's status comparison -- ambiguous. A raw.trade_history row carrying an unknown th_st_id is held as a whole under L1.unknown-codes and supplies no fact to any handoff; a held row keeps its place in the order of reports even though its content may not be read, so it can still be the earliest raw.trade_history row and hold the trade -- when every raw.trade_history row of a trade is held, the earliest of them is still the earliest report of that source, and the trade is held on that basis alone, without needing to read any of their th_st_id values. A trade any of whose placement-fixing facts -- placement, owning account, or order type -- would come from a held report is held under L1.hole.held-first-report-placement until answered: the earliest report of the source that supplies that fact is held, whatever another source's earliest report says. Until answered, this handoff supplies no placed_at value for such a trade, which is held and reported by inv.unknown_codes_held instead, together with inv.trade_held_first_report_unclaimed. A trade whose every received report is held is not yet known to this job.
handoffs.review_trigger: th_dts is found to record something other than the report's own event time, a historical-load trade is found to have held per-status reports beyond its anchored raw.trade_history rows, or two of a trade's raw.trade_history rows share the same th_dts

handoffs.necessity: L1.placement-moment (amended) requires the order's type to determine its first lifecycle event; raw.trade_cdc's t_tt_id is the brokerage's own recorded order-type code on the trade's first-encountered report, and this handoff takes that value only, never a later report's t_tt_id, mirroring owning_account_number's first_encounter_only handoff since raw.trade_history carries no order-type field either.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_tt_id on a trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report names the order's own type and is anchored by trade_code_meanings.trade_type_codes. A raw.trade_cdc row carrying any unknown code -- cdc_flag, t_st_id, or t_tt_id -- is held as a whole under L1.unknown-codes and supplies no fact to any handoff, not only this one; a held row keeps its place in the order of reports and can still be this trade's first-encountered report, holding the trade under L1.hole.held-first-report-placement without any of its content being read for this handoff's purposes, and a trade whose every received report is held is not yet known to this job. A trade any of whose placement-fixing facts -- placement, owning account, or order type -- would come from a held report is held under L1.hole.held-first-report-placement until answered: the earliest raw.trade_cdc report is held, whatever another source's earliest report says. Until answered, this handoff supplies no order_type value for such a trade, which is held and reported by inv.unknown_codes_held instead, together with inv.trade_held_first_report_unclaimed.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_tt_id is found to record a value outside {TLB, TLS, TMB, TMS}, or to change across reports of the same trade

handoffs.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership reference to name the account as it stood at the moment of placement; L1.as-of defines that answer as the latest statement that took effect at or before the queried moment. This handoff selects, among the upstream ownership-history statements of this trade's owning_account_number, the one whose effective_from is the latest at or before placed_at, and freezes that effective_from as the second half of the (account_number, effective_from) reference identifying the specific account statement -- not the account's current statement.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.account entity carries a resolvable statement of this trade's owning account with an effective_from at or before placed_at.
handoffs.review_trigger: no logical.account statement of the owning account has an effective_from at or before placed_at, or more than one candidate ties for latest

handoffs.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires that, through the account, the trade also belongs to the customer as that customer stood at the same moment; the account statement already pinned by owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from carries, as its own owning_customer_number, exactly that customer. This handoff freezes that same value directly off the pinned statement rather than performing an independent as-of lookup, so the customer named can never be inconsistent with the account statement this trade's ownership pins.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible wherever the account statement pinned by owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from itself has a resolvable owning_customer_number.
handoffs.review_trigger: the account statement pinned by owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from has no resolvable owning_customer_number

handoffs.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership reference to name the customer as they stood at the moment of placement, not the customer's current statement -- 'and through it the customer, as they stood'; L1.as-of defines that answer as the latest statement that took effect at or before the queried moment; L1.placement-moment fixes that moment to placed_at. This handoff selects, among ownership-history's logical.customer statements of the customer named by owning_customer_number, the one whose effective_from is the latest at or before placed_at, and freezes that effective_from as the second half of the (customer_number, effective_from) reference identifying the specific customer statement.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.customer entity carries a resolvable statement of the customer named by owning_customer_number with an effective_from at or before placed_at.
handoffs.review_trigger: no logical.customer statement of owning_customer_number has an effective_from at or before placed_at, or more than one candidate ties for latest

handoffs.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report of a trade to update its status; raw.trade_cdc's t_st_id is the brokerage's own recorded lifecycle-status value on each report of the trade.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_st_id on a trade_cdc row names the trade's lifecycle status as of that report, and is one of the anchored status_codes. A raw.trade_cdc row carrying any unknown code -- cdc_flag, t_st_id, or t_tt_id -- is held as a whole under L1.unknown-codes and supplies no fact to any handoff, not only this one; a held row is never a later report for this handoff's latest_change selection, and status stands as it last stood. The hold is reported by inv.unknown_codes_held, not this handoff.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_st_id is found to record something other than the trade's lifecycle status

handoffs.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's executed price; raw.trade_cdc's t_trade_price is the brokerage's own recorded executed-price value on each report, distinct from t_bid_price, which records the price at which the trade was requested rather than executed and this job does not hand off.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_trade_price on a trade_cdc row names the price at which the trade actually executed, as of that report. A raw.trade_cdc row carrying any unknown code -- cdc_flag, t_st_id, or t_tt_id -- is held as a whole under L1.unknown-codes and supplies no fact to any handoff, not only this one; a held row is never a later report for this handoff's latest_change selection, and executed_price stands as it last stood. The hold is reported by inv.unknown_codes_held, not this handoff.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_trade_price is found to record a requested price rather than an executed price

handoffs.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's fees; raw.trade_cdc's t_chrg is the brokerage's own recorded charge value on each report, the fees fact the clause names.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_chrg on a trade_cdc row names the fees the brokerage charges on the trade, as of that report. A raw.trade_cdc row carrying any unknown code -- cdc_flag, t_st_id, or t_tt_id -- is held as a whole under L1.unknown-codes and supplies no fact to any handoff, not only this one; a held row is never a later report for this handoff's latest_change selection, and fees stands as it last stood. The hold is reported by inv.unknown_codes_held, not this handoff.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_chrg is found to record something other than fees

handoffs.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's commission; raw.trade_cdc's t_comm is the brokerage's own recorded commission value on each report.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_comm on a trade_cdc row names the commission charged on the trade, as of that report. A raw.trade_cdc row carrying any unknown code -- cdc_flag, t_st_id, or t_tt_id -- is held as a whole under L1.unknown-codes and supplies no fact to any handoff, not only this one; a held row is never a later report for this handoff's latest_change selection, and commission stands as it last stood. The hold is reported by inv.unknown_codes_held, not this handoff.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_comm is found to record something other than commission

handoffs.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's tax; raw.trade_cdc's t_tax is the brokerage's own recorded tax value on each report.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_tax on a trade_cdc row names the tax owed on the trade, as of that report. A raw.trade_cdc row carrying any unknown code -- cdc_flag, t_st_id, or t_tt_id -- is held as a whole under L1.unknown-codes and supplies no fact to any handoff, not only this one; a held row is never a later report for this handoff's latest_change selection, and tax stands as it last stood. The hold is reported by inv.unknown_codes_held, not this handoff.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_tax is found to record something other than tax

handoffs.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's quantity; raw.trade_cdc's t_qty is the brokerage's own recorded quantity value on each report.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_qty on a trade_cdc row names the trade's quantity, as of that report. A raw.trade_cdc row carrying any unknown code -- cdc_flag, t_st_id, or t_tt_id -- is held as a whole under L1.unknown-codes and supplies no fact to any handoff, not only this one; a held row is never a later report for this handoff's latest_change selection, and quantity stands as it last stood. The hold is reported by inv.unknown_codes_held, not this handoff.
handoffs.review_trigger: t_qty is found to record something other than quantity

invariants.statement: For any trade_number, every anchored (not held under L1.unknown-codes) raw.trade_cdc report of that trade carries the same t_ca_id as the trade's first-encountered anchored report; owning_account_number is set once at that first anchored encounter and is never replaced by a later anchored report. A held report is not evidence either way: it neither confirms nor contradicts owning_account_number, and is excluded from this invariant's comparison entirely.
invariants.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement states directly that later changes do not move a trade that was already placed; this invariant is the restatement of that requirement over the account a trade is recorded against. L1.unknown-codes holds a report as a whole and lets nothing but its place in the order of reports be read, so a held report cannot confirm the frozen t_ca_id (its content is not read) nor contradict it (it is not treated as a later report carrying a different value); this invariant quantifies over anchored reports only.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while raw.trade_cdc never legitimately reassigns a trade to a different account after its first anchored report; a contradiction among anchored reports would indicate a data error or an unaddressed business rule, not a value this attribute should adopt. A held report supplies no t_ca_id value and is excluded from this comparison entirely, per L1.unknown-codes.
invariants.review_trigger: a later anchored raw.trade_cdc report of a known trade_number carries a t_ca_id different from the one recorded at first anchored encounter

invariants.statement: For any trade_number, placed_at, owning_account_effective_from, owning_customer_number, and owning_customer_effective_from are each set once -- from the trade's first-encountered anchored report and the account and customer statements resolved as of that report's own time -- and are never replaced by a later anchored report of the same trade. A held report is not evidence either way: it neither confirms nor contradicts these values, and is excluded from this invariant's comparison entirely.
invariants.necessity: L1.placement-moment fixes placement to the earliest held report's own time, and L1.attribution-at-placement states directly that later changes do not move a trade that was already placed; this invariant is the restatement of that requirement over the placement-moment reference attributes. L1.unknown-codes holds a report as a whole and lets nothing but its place in the order of reports be read, so a held report cannot confirm these frozen values (its content is not read) nor contradict them (it is not treated as a later report carrying a different value); this invariant quantifies over anchored reports only.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while a later anchored report of a known trade, from either anchored source (raw.trade_cdc or raw.trade_history), never carries an earlier event time than the one already recorded as placed_at. A held report supplies no event time and is excluded from this comparison entirely, per L1.unknown-codes.
invariants.review_trigger: a later anchored report of a known trade_number, from either anchored source, carries an event time earlier than its recorded placed_at, or any of placed_at, owning_account_effective_from, owning_customer_number, owning_customer_effective_from is found replaced after first encounter by an anchored report

invariants.statement: For any trade_number whose earliest report (across both anchored sources) is not held under L1.unknown-codes, placed_at equals th_dts of the trade's earliest raw.trade_history row when any raw.trade_history rows exist for that trade, and otherwise equals t_dts of the trade's earliest raw.trade_cdc row (smallest (batch_date, cdc_dsn)). A trade whose earliest report is itself held, with a later report that is not, is unclaimed by this invariant until L1.hole.held-first-report-placement is answered: it is held and reported by inv.unknown_codes_held, given no placed_at value and no logical.trade row by this job.
invariants.necessity: L1.placement-moment defines placement as the moment stated by the earliest report the brokerage holds, and the anchored trade_code_meanings.report_order states which row that is across the two anchored sources; inv.trade_placement_reference_frozen checks only that placed_at is set once and never replaced, not that the value it was set to is the correct earliest-report time. This invariant is the direct, checkable restatement of that correctness: without it, a placed_at wrongly fixed at a later report's time (for example, a historical-load trade's snapshot row instead of its earliest TradeHistory row) would still pass the 'set once' check.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while trade_code_meanings.report_order remains as anchored and every raw.trade_history row's th_dts and every raw.trade_cdc row's t_dts are each that row's own stated event time. L1.hole.held-first-report-placement bounds the case where a trade's earliest report is itself held and a later report is not: until answered, this invariant does not claim such a trade has any placed_at value at all, correct or otherwise.
invariants.review_trigger: a trade with anchored raw.trade_history rows has placed_at set to anything other than the smallest th_dts among them, or a trade with none has placed_at set to anything other than t_dts of its smallest-(batch_date, cdc_dsn) raw.trade_cdc row

invariants.statement: For any trade_number whose first-encountered report's status and order type are not held under L1.unknown-codes (per inv.unknown_codes_held) and that is not held as a market order seen pending (per inv.trade_market_order_seen_pending_held), first_seen_late is true if and only if the trade's first-encountered report -- across both anchored sources, its earliest raw.trade_history row if any exist, otherwise its earliest raw.trade_cdc row -- carries a status (th_st_id or t_st_id, respectively) later than order_type's first lifecycle event: PNDG for a limit order (TLB, TLS), per status_order's first entry; SBMT for a market order (TMB, TMS), per L1.placement-moment's amended sentence; using trade_code_meanings.status_order, trade_type_codes, and report_order to identify that first-encountered report and the order's type. An unknown code on a later report does not hold the first-encountered report and does not remove a trade from this invariant's claim.
invariants.necessity: L1.placement-moment (amended) defines first seen late by reference to whether the earliest held report is later than the trade's true first lifecycle stage, now order-type-dependent since an order sent straight to market has no pending stage; this invariant is the direct, checkable restatement of first_seen_late's own derivation rule over the trades it decides, leaving the two cases where the first-encountered report itself is held -- reported by inv.unknown_codes_held (its status or order type) and inv.trade_market_order_seen_pending_held -- to inv.trade_first_seen_late_defined_or_held instead; a held report elsewhere in the trade's history does not narrow this invariant's claim.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while trade_code_meanings.status_order, trade_type_codes, and report_order remain as anchored, and while order_type correctly reflects the trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report's t_tt_id.
invariants.review_trigger: for a trade whose first-encountered report's status and order type are not held under L1.unknown-codes and that is not held as a market order seen pending, first_seen_late is found true for one whose first-encountered report has status equal to its order_type's first lifecycle event, or false for one whose status is later than it

invariants.statement: For any trade_number, a later raw.trade_cdc report of that same trade with cdc_flag I or U, and with every one of its coded fields (cdc_flag, t_st_id, t_tt_id) anchored, replaces status, executed_price, fees, commission, tax, and quantity with its newly reported values on the same row; the trade_number itself is never replaced. A report with cdc_flag D is not a later report under this invariant: what it means for the trade's outcome is L1.hole.deletions, not decided here. A report held under L1.unknown-codes -- any one of its coded fields unanchored -- is likewise not a later report under this invariant: it is held as a whole, supplies no fact, and does not update the outcome; the hold is reported by inv.unknown_codes_held instead.
invariants.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome states directly that a later report of the same trade updates the outcome, describing that update entirely in terms of the trade's four named lifecycle statuses (pending, submitted, completed, cancelled); trade_code_meanings.cdc_flag anchors I as newly inserted and U as updating an existing record, both of which carry one of those statuses, so this invariant is the restatement of the update-in-place requirement over the six named outcome facts for I- and U-flagged reports specifically. L1.unknown-codes holds a report as a whole when any of its coded fields is unanchored; such a report changes nothing and creates nothing, so it cannot be the later report this invariant's update-in-place claim is about, exactly as a D-flagged report cannot.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while every I- or U-flagged raw.trade_cdc row for a given t_id is a later report about that same trade rather than an unrelated new trade reusing the number, and while such a row's other coded fields (t_st_id, t_tt_id) are anchored; a row with any unanchored coded field is held under L1.unknown-codes and is not a later report for this invariant, reported by inv.unknown_codes_held instead.
invariants.review_trigger: two I- or U-flagged raw.trade_cdc rows with the same t_id, both with fully anchored coded fields, are found to disagree in a way that suggests they describe different trades, or a row with an unanchored coded field is found to have updated the outcome

invariants.statement: This model defines no handoff sourced from a labeled constructed scenario for the trade entity, because chain/anchors/sources-v1.json anchors no ce.trade_* source; every trade statement this model can produce originates from the two anchored received sources, raw.trade_cdc and raw.trade_history, and from ownership-history's logical.account and logical.customer entities through the frozen ownership reference.
invariants.necessity: L1.constructed-scenarios requires a constructed scenario to be labeled wherever it appears and never mixed into received records; with no constructed trade source anchored, this job has no mechanism that could introduce an unlabeled constructed fact into the trade entity, satisfying the clause vacuously for this job as it stands.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Credible while sources-v1.json continues to anchor no labeled constructed source for trades; if one is added, this invariant and the model must be revisited.
invariants.review_trigger: sources-v1.json gains a ce.trade_* entry, or a trade statement is found to originate from anything other than raw.trade_cdc, raw.trade_history, or ownership-history's logical.account and logical.customer entities

invariants.statement: For any trade_number whose (owning_account_number, owning_account_effective_from) pair resolves, that pair identifies exactly one statement of ownership-history's logical.account entity, and that statement's own provenance value (non-null only when it is sourced from the labeled ce.account_changes scenario) is the provenance reachable for this trade.
invariants.necessity: L1.constructed-scenarios requires a constructed scenario to remain labeled wherever it appears; L1.attribution-at-placement is what fixes owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from as the frozen pair identifying the exact account statement a trade's ownership pins. Together they entail that the referenced statement's own provenance label -- if any -- stays reachable through that pair rather than needing a copy on the trade; this job defines no separate provenance attribute of its own that could omit, duplicate, or contradict it, and this invariant is the checkable restatement of the reachability that makes that omission safe.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while ownership-history's logical.account entity carries at most one statement per (account_number, effective_from), and while ownership-history's logical.customer entity, which now also feeds the frozen ownership reference through owning_customer_number and owning_customer_effective_from, carries at most one statement per (customer_number, effective_from). The customer pin cannot itself carry an unlabeled constructed fact: logical.customer has no provenance attribute of its own, and chain/anchors/sources-v1.json anchors no ce.customer_* source, so there is no labeled constructed customer scenario for one to be mislabeled or omitted from in the first place.
invariants.review_trigger: the pair (owning_account_number, owning_account_effective_from) for a trade resolves to zero or more than one ownership-history account statement, the pair (owning_customer_number, owning_customer_effective_from) resolves to zero or more than one ownership-history customer statement, or sources-v1.json gains a ce.customer_* source, or logical.customer gains a provenance value

invariants.statement: For any persisted logical.trade row, owning_account_number, owning_account_effective_from, owning_customer_number, and owning_customer_effective_from are each non-null.
invariants.necessity: owning_account_number, owning_account_effective_from, owning_customer_number, and owning_customer_effective_from are each declared nullable: false because L1.attribution-at-placement requires a trade's ownership to be the account, and through it the customer, as they stood at placement -- a reference, not merely a value that may be present when convenient -- and L1.as-of together with L1.placement-moment defines that reference as the account's and customer's statements in effect at placed_at. The two as_of_event_time handoffs that complete this reference (logical.account.effective_from -> owning_account_effective_from and logical.customer.effective_from -> owning_customer_effective_from) are each credible only while a qualifying statement exists at or before placed_at. This invariant is the direct, checkable restatement of those four nullable: false declarations and that shared assumption: it decides nothing about what happens when a trade's pin does not resolve, only that a persisted trade carrying any of the four references as null is a violation an audit can name, rather than a silent gap invisible to compare.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while the four pin attributes' nullable: false declaration continues to state this job's intent that every persisted trade carries the reference in full; whether a trade whose pin cannot resolve should instead be persisted with the reference incomplete, dropped entirely, or handled some other way is not decided by this invariant and stays open under L1.hole.change-effective-time, which already bounds the statements this reference resolves against.
invariants.review_trigger: a persisted logical.trade row carries owning_account_number, owning_account_effective_from, owning_customer_number, or owning_customer_effective_from as null

invariants.statement: For any trade_number that has at least one received raw.trade_cdc report whose coded fields (cdc_flag, t_st_id, t_tt_id) are all anchored and that does not carry cdc_flag D, and none of whose placement-fixing facts (placement, owning account, or order type) would come from a held report, exactly one logical.trade row exists for that trade_number. A trade_number with any cdc_flag D report among its received raw.trade_cdc reports is L1.hole.deletions' case and is not claimed by this invariant. A trade_number known only through reports held under L1.unknown-codes, or known only through raw.trade_history rows (raw.trade_history alone carries no identity handoff and cannot by itself establish a logical.trade row), is not yet known to this job and is not claimed by this invariant either; inv.unknown_codes_held reports each held report instead. A trade_number any of whose placement-fixing facts would come from a held report -- the earliest report of the source that supplies that fact is held, whatever another source's earliest report says -- is likewise not yet claimed, pending L1.hole.held-first-report-placement; inv.trade_held_first_report_unclaimed makes this the audit's own checkable claim, and inv.trade_placed_at_matches_earliest_report and inv.trade_first_seen_late_defined_or_held agree.
invariants.necessity: L1.identity requires a trade_number the brokerage already identifies to be the same persistent thing across every report of it, not a thing this job may simply fail to track. This invariant restates that persistence requirement as completeness rather than only as consistency (which inv.trade_owning_account_frozen and sg.trade-identity's own coverage already check): every trade_number that has at least one received raw.trade_cdc report with fully anchored codes and no cdc_flag D, and whose earliest report is not itself held, must appear as exactly one logical.trade row; a trade_number with any cdc_flag D report is L1.hole.deletions' case and is not claimed here. raw.trade_history alone cannot satisfy this invariant's existential: the entity's only identity handoff is raw.trade_cdc.t_id -> trade_number, so a trade_number known only through raw.trade_history rows, with no raw.trade_cdc report at all, has no handoff that could ever produce trade_number for it, and is not claimed here either. A trade this job cannot pin (sg.placement-moment) is therefore a violation this invariant names, not a row the job is silently permitted to omit; together with inv.trade_ownership_pin_present, a trade whose pin does not resolve fires the same violation on every engine projection instead of being decided differently by whichever join shape a projection happens to use. L1.unknown-codes' clarification that a held report changes nothing and creates nothing, and that a trade known only through held reports is not yet known to the job, is why this invariant does not claim such a trade; inv.unknown_codes_held reports the held report(s) instead, not this invariant. L1.hole.held-first-report-placement bounds a trade any of whose placement-fixing facts (placement, owning account, or order type) would come from a held report: until answered, this invariant does not claim it either, agreeing with inv.trade_placed_at_matches_earliest_report, inv.trade_first_seen_late_defined_or_held, and inv.trade_held_first_report_unclaimed, which makes the absence its own checkable audit.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while every raw.trade_cdc row with cdc_flag I or U, and every raw.trade_history row, reports a trade_number the business considers a real, receivable trade, and while a trade with at least one raw.trade_cdc report whose coded fields are all anchored is correctly distinguished from one whose received reports are all held. L1.hole.deletions bounds what a cdc_flag D report means for a trade's persistence -- whether its trade_number must still appear as a row, must be removed, or something else -- so this invariant is quantified only over trade_numbers none of whose received raw.trade_cdc reports carries cdc_flag D at all, leaving a trade_number with any D report entirely to that hole, not merely excluding the D-flagged report itself from an otherwise-qualifying trade. The anchored trade_code_meanings.report_order.note states that a historical-load trade's held reports are its TradeHistory rows together with the snapshot Trade row, so every th_t_id also appears as a Batch1 t_id (cdc_flag I, cdc_dsn 0); this invariant's coverage of a historical-load trade therefore rests on that same snapshot row's raw.trade_cdc report, not on a raw.trade_history handoff this model does not define. L1.hole.held-first-report-placement bounds a trade any of whose placement-fixing facts would come from a held report; until answered, this invariant does not claim a row for it.
invariants.review_trigger: a trade_number that has at least one received raw.trade_cdc report with fully anchored codes, no cdc_flag D report, and no placement-fixing fact from a held report does not appear as exactly one logical.trade row, a th_t_id appears in raw.trade_history with no corresponding t_id row in any batch of raw.trade_cdc, a trade_number known only through reports held under L1.unknown-codes appears as a logical.trade row, or a trade_number any of whose placement-fixing facts would come from a held report appears as a logical.trade row before L1.hole.held-first-report-placement is answered

invariants.statement: For any trade_number that inv.every_received_trade_persisted claims a logical.trade row for, first_seen_late is null if and only if the trade is held: either inv.unknown_codes_held reports its first-encountered report's status or order type as outside the anchored vocabularies, or inv.trade_market_order_seen_pending_held reports it as a market order first reported PNDG. first_seen_late is non-null (true or false) for every other such trade. A trade_number any of whose placement-fixing facts (placement, owning account, or order type) would come from a held report is not claimed by inv.every_received_trade_persisted at all, pending L1.hole.held-first-report-placement, and so has no first_seen_late value for this invariant to claim either.
invariants.necessity: L1.unknown-codes and L1.hole.market-order-seen-pending together carve out the two cases L1.placement-moment's amended rule does not decide; this invariant is the direct, checkable restatement that first_seen_late's nullability tracks exactly those two held sets and no others -- a trade is not left null for any other reason, and is not decided (true or false) for either of these two. It agrees with inv.every_received_trade_persisted, inv.trade_placed_at_matches_earliest_report, and inv.trade_held_first_report_unclaimed that a trade any of whose placement-fixing facts would come from a held report is unclaimed under L1.hole.held-first-report-placement rather than given first_seen_late null: such a trade has no logical.trade row at all, not a row with a null flag.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while inv.unknown_codes_held and inv.trade_market_order_seen_pending_held together enumerate every case this job holds rather than decides among trades inv.every_received_trade_persisted claims; a third undecided case would need its own hole and its own held-invariant before this one could still hold. L1.hole.held-first-report-placement bounds a trade this invariant does not reach at all, since inv.every_received_trade_persisted (and inv.trade_held_first_report_unclaimed) does not claim it a row in the first place.
invariants.review_trigger: first_seen_late is null for a claimed trade neither invariant reports as held, non-null for a claimed trade either invariant reports as held, or present at all for a trade inv.every_received_trade_persisted does not claim

invariants.statement: For any trade_number whose order_type is TMB or TMS (a market order) and whose first-encountered report -- across both anchored sources -- carries status PNDG, this invariant reports the trade as held for review under L1.hole.market-order-seen-pending; first_seen_late for such a trade is null, not true or false.
invariants.necessity: L1.hole.market-order-seen-pending leaves undecided whether a market order's earliest held report at PNDG is a late first encounter, a mis-typed order, or a record error, since L1.placement-moment's amended sentence says a market order has no pending stage at all; this invariant is the checkable restatement of the hole's own instruction to hold such a trade for review rather than decide it either way.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while trade_code_meanings.trade_type_codes and status_codes remain as anchored and order_type and the first-encountered report's status are each correctly determined; this invariant reports a trade held, it does not resolve the hole.
invariants.review_trigger: a market order (TMB, TMS) whose first-encountered report carries status PNDG is not reported as held, or a trade reported as held under this invariant is not a market order first reported PNDG

invariants.statement: For any trade_number whose earliest report of either anchored source (raw.trade_cdc or raw.trade_history) is held under L1.unknown-codes, or any of whose placement-fixing facts (placement, owning account, or order type) would come from a held report -- the earliest report of the source that supplies that fact is held, whatever another source's earliest report says -- no logical.trade row exists for that trade_number; the trade is reported by inv.unknown_codes_held instead.
invariants.necessity: L1.hole.held-first-report-placement holds a trade any of whose placement-fixing facts would come from a held report, until the hole is answered; L1.unknown-codes' clarification that a held report changes nothing and creates nothing is why such a trade has no row at all, not a row with placeholder or carried-forward values. inv.every_received_trade_persisted, inv.trade_placed_at_matches_earliest_report, and inv.trade_first_seen_late_defined_or_held each already agree that such a trade is unclaimed; this invariant is the direct, checkable restatement of that absence as its own audit, distinct from those invariants' own claims about what a row looks like when one is claimed, so no engine projection can silently supply a row for a trade this hole holds by leaving the absence itself unaudited.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while L1.hole.held-first-report-placement remains open and inv.unknown_codes_held correctly identifies which of a trade's reports are held; once the hole is answered, this invariant's claim -- that no row exists -- may need to be revisited or retired depending on the answer.
invariants.review_trigger: a trade_number whose earliest report of either anchored source is held, or any of whose placement-fixing facts would come from a held report, appears as a logical.trade row

invariants.statement: For any trade_number, order_type equals t_tt_id on the trade's first-encountered anchored raw.trade_cdc report, and is never replaced by a later anchored report's t_tt_id. A held report is not evidence either way: it neither confirms nor contradicts order_type, and is excluded from this invariant's comparison entirely.
invariants.necessity: order_type's own type element cites L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome's enumeration of the outcome facts a later report changes (status, executed price, fees, commission, tax, quantity) and its statement that a later report leaves the ownership as first recorded; order type is in neither set, so nothing a later report does moves it. This invariant is stated like inv.trade_owning_account_frozen -- checking every anchored report for agreement with the first-encountered one, not only that the first-encountered value is never replaced -- because an order's type (limit or market, buy or sell) is fixed at placement by the same brokerage convention that fixes the owning account: neither trade_code_meanings nor the Sketch names a legitimate later correction to an order's type, unlike status, which L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names directly as mutable outcome. A disagreement among a trade's anchored reports about t_tt_id therefore indicates a data error, not a value this attribute should adopt, so both engines check the one stronger proposition rather than two engines each choosing a different, weaker one. This invariant is the direct, checkable restatement of that freeze -- order_type equals the trade's first-encountered anchored raw.trade_cdc report's t_tt_id and is never replaced -- as its own audit, exactly as inv.trade_owning_account_frozen restates the analogous freeze for owning_account_number, so an L3 audit need not embed the check inside another invariant's own audit. L1.unknown-codes holds a report as a whole and lets nothing but its place in the order of reports be read, so a held report cannot confirm the frozen order_type (its content is not read) nor contradict it; this invariant quantifies over anchored reports only.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while t_tt_id on a trade's first-encountered anchored raw.trade_cdc report is the order's own type and is never legitimately corrected by a later anchored report. A held report supplies no t_tt_id value and is excluded from this comparison entirely, per L1.unknown-codes.
invariants.review_trigger: a later anchored raw.trade_cdc report of a known trade_number carries a t_tt_id different from the one recorded at first anchored encounter

invariants.statement: For every raw.trade_cdc row this job consumes, cdc_flag is one of {I, U, D}, t_st_id is one of {PNDG, SBMT, CMPT, CNCL}, and t_tt_id is one of {TLB, TLS, TMB, TMS}; for every raw.trade_history row this job consumes, th_st_id is one of {PNDG, SBMT, CMPT, CNCL}. A row carrying a value outside its field's anchored vocabulary is a violation of this invariant, naming the record and the code; it is held for review, not interpreted, defaulted, or dropped.
invariants.necessity: L1.unknown-codes requires every job to report, as a violation naming the record and the code, any consumed row whose coded field carries a value its anchored vocabulary does not name, and forbids interpreting, defaulting, or dropping it. This job reads three anchored code vocabularies across its two consumed sources -- cdc_flag and t_tt_id on raw.trade_cdc, and the shared status_codes vocabulary on both t_st_id (raw.trade_cdc) and th_st_id (raw.trade_history) -- and this invariant is the direct, checkable restatement of that reporting duty over all three; it says nothing about what happens to a held record afterward, which is each derivation's or handoff's own parallel_assumption to state, and, for first_seen_late specifically, L1.hole.market-order-seen-pending's neighbor.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while trade_code_meanings.status_codes, trade_type_codes, and cdc_flag remain as anchored and exhaustively enumerate the codes each field may carry; a row whose coded field falls outside its vocabulary is not decided by this job to be an error, a future code, or something else -- only reported.
invariants.review_trigger: a raw.trade_cdc row carries a cdc_flag outside {I, U, D}, a t_st_id outside {PNDG, SBMT, CMPT, CNCL}, or a t_tt_id outside {TLB, TLS, TMB, TMS}; or a raw.trade_history row carries a th_st_id outside {PNDG, SBMT, CMPT, CNCL}

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: logical.trade's history kind, incremental_by_identity, is the direct consequence of L1.identity (a trade is a persistent identified thing; a later report about the same trade number is the same trade, not a new one), L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome (a later report updates outcome facts on this same row), and L1.attribution-at-placement (the trade's ownership, once established at placement, is never moved by a later report about the account or customer) -- together these entail one row per trade_number, updated in place, holding a frozen portion beside a mutable portion. The frozen portion's account-identity component is owning_account_number: raw.trade_cdc's t_ca_id, taken only from the trade's first-encountered report and never replaced by a later one, which inv.trade_owning_account_frozen restates directly. This is the part of L1.attribution-at-placement that names which account a trade belongs to, fixed at first encounter; the remaining part -- which dated statement of that account, and through it which customer, stood as of the moment of placement -- is now resolved by L1.placement-moment and covered by sg.placement-moment instead, since that is the more specific claim. This group's own scope is limited to the entity's shape and the account-identity portion.
