That portion is nonetheless bounded: owning_account_number is taken from the trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report, identified by the anchored trade_code_meanings.report_order (batch_date, cdc_dsn) -- file production order -- not from a report carrying which file delivered it, which L1.hole.batch-identity leaves open. It is also bounded by L1.hole.deletions: what a cdc_flag D row means is undecided, including whether the trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report could itself be D-flagged and what that would mean for owning_account_number.
sufficiency_groups.gap: L1.hole.batch-identity bounds owning_account_number's reliance on report_order rather than a report carrying which file delivered it; L1.hole.deletions bounds what a D-flagged first-encountered report would mean for owning_account_number.

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: L1.placement-moment fixes placement to the moment stated by the trade's earliest held report, in that report's own time. placed_at is handed off, under selector first_encounter_only, from whichever anchored source holds that earliest report: raw.trade_cdc's t_dts for a trade whose held reports are Trade change records ordered by trade_code_meanings.report_order's (batch_date, cdc_dsn), or, for a historical-load trade with anchored raw.trade_history rows, raw.trade_history's th_dts on its earliest such row instead, per report_order's statement that such a trade's earliest held report is its earliest TradeHistory row, not its Trade snapshot; inv.trade_placed_at_matches_earliest_report makes this rule itself checkable, not merely that placed_at is set once. Together the two handoffs carry exactly that moment, frozen, across both anchored report sources; owning_account_number still comes only from raw.trade_cdc's t_ca_id regardless of which source supplies placed_at, since raw.trade_history carries no account field (sg.trade-shape). L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership reference to be the pair of statements, account and customer, as they stood at that moment -- 'the account, and through it the customer, as they stood at the moment the trade was placed' -- not either one's current statement. L1.as-of defines each such answer as the upstream statement whose effective_from is the latest at or before placed_at; L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome's 'leaves the ownership as first recorded' is what fixes owning_account_effective_from, owning_customer_number, and owning_customer_effective_from as frozen_from_first_encounter on this entity rather than per_statement, since that role belongs to the account and customer entities they are drawn from, not to how they behave once pinned here. owning_account_effective_from, handed off from logical.account.effective_from with selector as_of_event_time, completes the (account_number, effective_from) pair with owning_account_number (sg.trade-shape) that identifies the exact account statement. owning_customer_number is handed off directly from that same pinned account statement's own logical.account.owning_customer_number, so it can never name a customer inconsistent with it; owning_customer_effective_from, handed off from logical.customer.effective_from with selector as_of_event_time (also at or before placed_at), completes the (customer_number, effective_from) pair identifying the exact customer statement, satisfying the 'and through it the customer, as they stood' half of the clause in full -- not just which customer, but which of that customer's dated statements. inv.trade_placement_reference_frozen restates that all four reference attributes are set once, at first encounter, and never replaced. inv.trade_ownership_pin_present restates, as a single checkable fact, that a persisted trade never carries a null in any of these four attributes -- that the pin resolved, not merely that whatever it resolved to is frozen. first_seen_late, using trade_code_meanings.status_order and report_order together with order_type (handed off from raw.trade_cdc.t_tt_id under selector first_encounter_only and anchored, as to which codes exist and which are market or limit, by trade_code_meanings.trade_type_codes), marks a trade whose first-encountered report -- across both anchored sources -- as first seen late when its status (th_st_id or t_st_id) is later than its order type's first lifecycle event: PNDG, status_order's first entry, for a limit order (TLB, TLS); SBMT for a market order (TMB, TMS), per L1.placement-moment's amended sentence that an order sent straight to market has no pending stage; so a limit order first reported anything other than PNDG is first seen late, a market order first reported SBMT is not, and one first reported CMPT or CNCL is -- a market order first reported PNDG, and an order type outside the anchored four, are left undefined by this rule and are not claimed by inv.trade_first_seen_late_matches_status_order, which otherwise restates it directly. This coverage is conditional, not complete: L1.hole.change-effective-time bounds the account- and customer-statement pins against any upstream statement ownership-history has deferred (a CDC-sourced account or customer update); L1.hole.batch-identity bounds whether a report would also need to carry which file delivered it, which first_encounter_only and latest_change currently answer only via file production order (report_order) or, for raw.trade_history, th_dts ordering, not batch identity; L1.hole.closed-account-activity bounds a pin that lands on a closed-account statement whose status this job cannot verify against the trade's own later activity; L1.hole.deletions bounds what a cdc_flag D row means for a trade's first-encountered report and hence for placed_at and first_seen_late. Separately, L1.hole.owner-change-reversions-account (recorded in holes) could change which account statement placed_at pins if its resolution re-versions accounts on a customer-only change.
sufficiency_groups.gap: L1.hole.change-effective-time, L1.hole.batch-identity, L1.hole.closed-account-activity, L1.hole.deletions, L1.hole.owner-change-reversions-account, L1.hole.market-order-seen-pending, and L1.hole.held-first-report-placement each bound part of this group's coverage; see coverage_claim.

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: Every raw.trade_cdc row carries t_id, the brokerage's own trade number, handed off unchanged into trade_number with the identity mutation role; because this value is identical across every CDC row reporting the same trade, no later report ever produces a 'different' trade, satisfying L1.identity's persistence requirement for the trade entity. inv.every_received_trade_persisted extends this group's claim from consistency to completeness: every trade_number none of whose received reports carries cdc_flag D appears as exactly one logical.trade row, not zero and not more than one.
sufficiency_groups.gap: L1.hole.deletions bounds this group's completeness claim: a trade_number with any cdc_flag D report is not claimed by inv.every_received_trade_persisted and stays that hole's case.

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome enumerates exactly six outcome facts -- status, executed price, fees, commission, tax, quantity -- that change as a trade moves through its life, describing that change entirely in terms of the trade's four named lifecycle statuses (pending, submitted, completed, cancelled). Each fact is handed off from raw.trade_cdc's own field for that fact (t_st_id, t_trade_price, t_chrg, t_comm, t_tax, t_qty respectively), typed mutable, with selector latest_change ordering candidate reports by the anchored trade_code_meanings.report_order (batch_date, cdc_dsn) -- file production order, not a report carrying which file delivered it, which L1.hole.batch-identity leaves open. The anchored trade_code_meanings.cdc_flag states I as newly inserted and U as updating an existing record; both carry one of the clause's four named statuses, so latest_change's candidate set is I- and U-flagged reports, which inv.trade_outcome_updates_in_place restates directly. A cdc_flag D report is not one of these: 'deleted' is not a status the clause names, so latest_change does not select an outcome value from a D-flagged report; what a D-flagged report means for the trade's outcome -- whether it stands, is voided, or something else -- is L1.hole.deletions, not decided by this exclusion. All six facts the clause names are otherwise covered by a member of this group; the clause names no others.
sufficiency_groups.gap: L1.hole.deletions bounds what a D-flagged report means for a trade's outcome; L1.hole.batch-identity bounds latest_change's reliance on file production order rather than a report carrying which file delivered it.

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: chain/anchors/sources-v1.json anchors no labeled constructed source for trades (only ce.account_changes exists, and that is for accounts); this job therefore has no handoff that could mix an unlabeled constructed fact into the trade entity, which inv.trade_not_constructed restates: every trade statement this model can produce originates from the two anchored received sources (raw.trade_cdc and raw.trade_history) and, through the frozen ownership reference, ownership-history's logical.account and logical.customer entities. Separately, owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from (frozen_from_first_encounter, sg.trade-shape and sg.placement-moment) are the (account_number, effective_from) pair fixed by L1.attribution-at-placement that identifies the exact upstream ownership-history statement a trade's ownership pins; for any trade whose pin resolves to such a statement, inv.trade_ownership_provenance_reachable makes checkable that this pair reaches that statement's own provenance value (populated only when it is sourced from the labeled ce.account_changes scenario), so a trade whose ownership pins a constructed account statement has that label reachable through the pair, without this job needing, or introducing, a separate trade-level provenance attribute that could omit, duplicate, or contradict it. The customer pin (owning_customer_number, owning_customer_effective_from) raises no equivalent risk: logical.customer carries no provenance attribute of its own, and sources-v1.json anchors no ce.customer_* source, so there is no labeled constructed customer scenario for the customer pin to fail to relabel or duplicate. This claim is scoped to trades whose pins resolve; a trade whose pins do not yet resolve (bounded by L1.hole.change-effective-time, already sg.placement-moment's gap) has no pinned statements to reach a provenance value from in the first place, which is not a further gap of this group's own claim.

L1.unknown-codes requires every job to report a consumed row whose coded field carries a value its anchored vocabulary does not name, naming the record and the code, and forbids interpreting, defaulting, or dropping it; a held report changes nothing and creates nothing, so a trade known only through held reports is not yet known to this job. This job reads three anchored code vocabularies across its two consumed sources -- cdc_flag and t_tt_id on raw.trade_cdc, and the shared status_codes vocabulary on both t_st_id (raw.trade_cdc) and th_st_id (raw.trade_history) -- and inv.unknown_codes_held is the single checkable restatement of that reporting duty across all of them. Ten handoffs in this job read a coded field, each stating in its own parallel_assumption that a held row or report is not read as a fact by this handoff (a held later report is not a later report for latest_change and the value stands as last derived; a held row is not a first-encountered report for first_encounter_only and a trade known only through held rows is not yet known; an unanchored code on a value-carrying field yields no derived fact) and listing this invariant in its feedback: raw.trade_cdc.t_id->trade_number, raw.trade_cdc.t_ca_id->owning_account_number, and raw.trade_cdc.t_dts->placed_at (selection, reading cdc_flag); raw.trade_cdc.t_tt_id->order_type (its own field) and raw.trade_cdc.t_st_id->status (its own field, and cdc_flag for latest_change); and raw.trade_cdc.t_trade_price->executed_price, t_chrg->fees, t_comm->commission, t_tax->tax, and t_qty->quantity (cdc_flag, for latest_change). Adjacent to this group's own claim, first_seen_late (sg.placement-moment) carries the held case further: a first-encountered report held under this clause makes first_seen_late null, reported by inv.unknown_codes_held together with inv.trade_first_seen_late_defined_or_held; L1.hole.market-order-seen-pending bounds a distinct case -- PNDG is itself an anchored status, so a market order first reported PNDG is not an unknown code, and inv.unknown_codes_held does not report it, inv.trade_market_order_seen_pending_held (sg.placement-moment) does. Neither is a gap of this group's own claim, which is complete over the three vocabularies and their ten readers. This invariant decides nothing about what an unnamed record subsequently means.

holes.question: L1.placement-moment now settles placement, and anchored raw.trade_history now supplies the brokerage's own per-status times (th_dts per lifecycle stage, including CMPT) for historical-load trades, so this hole is purely the completion-policy question: which moment counts as 'when it completed,' and what a report should do with it, when a later report of a trade arrives without its full history? Having a time is not the same as knowing what reporting on completion means. This job does not model a completed-at moment, so nothing here is currently blocked by it, but it is carried because a future completion-timing attribute would need it answered.

Trades appear on accounts the brokerage recorded as closed years earlier. Is that a data error, a reopening the records omit, or does a closed account still own trades? Until answered, a trade's ownership reference (once resolvable) may point to an account statement whose closed status this job cannot verify against the trade's own later activity.

Does a change recorded in an incremental account or customer change file take effect at the file's batch date, or at some other moment? Until answered, some account and customer statements this job's owning_account_effective_from, owning_customer_number, and owning_customer_effective_from handoffs would need to resolve a trade's as-of ownership against remain unavailable, per ownership-history's own deferred handoffs from raw.account_cdc and raw.customer_cdc. A trade whose pin does not resolve is not dropped and not persisted with gaps by this job; it is surfaced as a violation of inv.trade_ownership_pin_present and inv.every_received_trade_persisted, and it is for the business to decide what happens to such a trade.

What does a deletion marker (cdc_flag D) in raw.trade_cdc mean for a trade's history, its recorded ownership, and the outcome facts this job carries? Anchored trade_code_meanings state I and U's meanings but leave D's meaning to this hole. This job's current handling -- excluding D-flagged reports from latest_change's candidate set, so the last I- or U-flagged outcome stands -- is provisional, pending this hole's resolution; it does not decide what a D-flagged report means for the trade otherwise, whether it stands, is voided, or something else, nor what it would mean if a trade's first-encountered report were itself D-flagged.

Securities, companies, and brokers are named on raw.trade_cdc (t_s_symb, t_exec_name) but not yet part of any job; when they are, the attribution rule must be restated for them. This job hands off neither field.

Does a report need to know which incremental file first delivered it? This job's first_encounter_only and latest_change selectors, and first_seen_late's derivation, rest on the anchored trade_code_meanings.report_order: for raw.trade_cdc rows, (batch_date, cdc_dsn) -- file production order; for raw.trade_history rows, the row's own th_dts value directly, not a file-order position. Neither rests on a report carrying which file delivered it. That ordering is enough to select a first-encountered or latest report today, but this hole stays open about whether a report also needs to carry its own delivering file, which would matter if production order (or th_dts) and delivery order could ever diverge.

When a customer's standing changes, does the brokerage consider every account of that customer to have a new statement at that moment, or only the customer? This job does not decide it, but its resolution could change which account statement placed_at pins: if an owner-side change also re-versions the account, a trade placed shortly after such a change could pin a different (later) account statement than it does today.

L1.placement-moment says an order sent straight to market has no pending stage. What does it mean when a market order's earliest held report is pending: a late first encounter, a mis-typed order, or a record error? Until answered, no job may decide whether such a trade is first seen late; it is held for review and reported like an unknown code, per inv.trade_market_order_seen_pending_held.

When a trade's earliest report is held under L1.unknown-codes and a later report is not, is the trade placed at the earliest report this job can read, or is the trade itself held until the first report is resolved? The same question arises for every fact fixed at placement: if the earliest report that would supply the owning account or the order type is held while an earlier report of another kind is not, may a later report supply it? L1.placement-moment speaks of the earliest report the brokerage holds; a held report is one the brokerage has but may not read. Until answered, a trade any of whose placement-fixing facts (placement, owning account, or order type) would come from a held report -- the earliest report of the source that supplies that fact is held, whatever another source's earliest report says -- is held: this job gives it no placed_at, owning_account_number, or order_type value and no logical.trade row; it is held and reported by inv.unknown_codes_held, agreeing with inv.every_received_trade_persisted and inv.trade_first_seen_late_defined_or_held.
